item.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 hits record one light-day distance, 50 years after launch
item.description:
This illustration shows Voyager 1 passing by the rings of Saturn. NASA/Hulton Archive/Getty Images In the summer of 2027, the Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 spacecraft will each reach a milestone in time. On Sept. 5 and Aug. 20, respectively, they will each have spent 50 years in space . During their journeys, they first explored the planets of the outer solar system, then traveled to the edge of the solar system. Eventually, they passed into the interstellar medium : the space between stars. Although not the first spacecraft ever launched, these are now the two oldest spacecraft still operating. But before the spacecraft hit their semicentennial, Voyager 1 will also reach a milestone in distance. On Nov. 18, 2026, at 5:16 a.m. EST, Voyager 1 will become the first human-built object of any kind to reach a distance of one light-day from Earth . At that point, it will have traveled about 16…

item.title: The Guardian view on the Trump, Xi and Putin meeting: it may be a first, but it’s not progress | Editorial
item.description:
A trilateral gathering is good news for China and Russia, but bad for the US – and its traditional allies “Historic” is a neutral descriptor, not a favourable one. Things can be unprecedented for good reason. Donald Trump’s meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China on Thursday will be the first time that the leaders of the US, China and Russia have gathered for talks as a trio. The trilateral on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit is striking, but it is not an achievement. The lack of a clear agenda is telling: the spectacle really is the substance. Mr Trump sees international affairs in terms of spheres of influence. This meeting reinforces the obvious conclusion for the rest of the world – that they don’t get to sit at the table, only to be on the plate. Mr Xi promotes the notion of a multipolar world. item.title: It Feels Like Everything is Breaking, and It’s Not Even Hackers
item.description:
You know things are bad when panic-buyers start emptying the shelves at Costco. As you might have noticed, everything is breaking. Over the past week, Outlook has gone down, U.S. air traffic control has gone down, banking systems have gone down, and the National Security Agency’s confidential-telephone system has gone down, and just today, Apple announced that some of its services are down. There is an air of something nefarious afoot. “If this is all a coincidence,” Senator Josh Hawley of Missouri said yesterday, “it’s like the greatest coincidence in the history of the world.” Others have traded apocalyptic theories: Are rogue AI agents taking over everything? item.title: Israeli tanks cross ‘yellow line’ boundary into Hamas-controlled central Gaza
item.description:
First incursion across boundary since ceasefire deal comes as Eisenkot seeks to form government without Netanyahu The Israeli military crossed into Hamas-controlled central Gaza on Wednesday in its first ground operation across the “yellow line” boundary since a fragile ceasefire was agreed last October, forcing dozens of displaced Palestinians to flee their tents. Israeli tanks rolled along the Salah al-Din road , Gaza’s main north-south route, a day after the US-backed Board of Peace, a body overseeing the ceasefire, accused Israel and Hamas of failing to honour their commitments to end hostilities. item.title: MLB commissioner Manfred cites fan support for salary cap as baseball heads towards lockout
item.description:
This article was written by Jason Foster and published on Sport & State , a new media company founded by Clay Travis that is built around sports, culture, original voices, and live conversation. * * * * * We’re about two weeks from a near-certain MLB lockout , and here’s what we know: The players do not want a salary cap . What we don’t know is what the players do want. As the Dec. 1 expiration of the current collective bargaining agreement approaches, the MLB Players Association has yet to offer any public counter-proposal to a salary cap.
